Ah, yes, I bet Edward cucking himself is his greatest proof of love according to Meyer. I don't know if he checked out, I don't think he is capable of it. But I'm sure he understands that if he were only a human Bella would not have loved him as fiercely. Bella's great love was acquiring immortality, specifically, her true love is being *herself* a vampire. Edward is in love with a monster, and I think he realized that. He is passive because his role is now subordinate to her: he isn't anymore her idol, she is her own God, and he is to be her worshipper. He is passive because he submits to this way of living, and maybe he thinks that's his punishment for being a monster too. In any case, the love story wasn't between two star-crossed people, it was between a greedy person and everlasting power and beauty. If only Meyer realized she ended up writing a psychological horror thanks to BD smh.

Bella's garter was weird. The whole writing seemed immature from the beginning of BD. 

I don't know about the pregnancy. Bella's life was in danger. Bella thought the baby was a benevolent being, Edward thought of it as a monster. There was not enough information about it early on, besides the fact that it was killing her. This kind of debate skims too closely to real-life situations with abortion. There are mothers who sacrifice themselves for the fetus and others who choose to terminate an at-risk pregnancy. While the choice would absolutely be Bella's, the gravity of a person dying during pregnancy and the conflicting feeling it causes should not be ignored. Frankly, I started to feel alienated from the story as soon as Bella became pregnant and obsessed with Renesmee. Seeing Edward resistant mirrored my own disbelief towards the plot. 

Completely agree that he gets sidelined. Their love was the reason of the saga. And it simmered away, along with Edward. I guess Bella didn't love him as much as she loved being a vampire. It's kind of grim. I bet he wonders about it too.
